source.title: Deep Double Descent for Time Series Forecasting: Avoiding Undertrained Models
source.authors: Valentino Assandri; Sam Heshmati; Burhaneddin Yaman; А. Яковлев; Ariel Emiliano Repetur

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests epoch-wise double descent on time-series forecasting models, using different datasets and model architectures and primarily validation-loss curves rather than the original setting and test-error measure.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly describes epoch-wise validation-loss curves for Autoformer on Exchange, Informer on Traffic, and Informer on ILI. Table 1 also compares test metrics from the original 10-epoch training schema with results after longer training, but these endpoint comparisons do not show the fall-rise-fall trajectory; the paper's reported aggregate comparison is recorded as a result that cannot determine that trajectory. The many separate Table 1 benchmark entries are not extracted as rows because they compare endpoints rather than the curve shape.
record.test_reason: The study trains three time-series Transformers (FEDformer, Autoformer, Informer) far longer than usual, up to 1000 epochs, on nine forecasting benchmarks. It reports validation-loss curves over epochs, some showing a fall-rise-fall shape. This is the epoch-wise test (V2) in a new setting (time-series forecasting). The measure is validation loss rather than test error, and the paper presents selected curves rather than a systematic count.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that epoch-wise deep double descent can occur on standard time-series benchmarks, that low-patience, short-epoch early stopping can leave models undertrained, and that longer training sets new state-of-the-art on about 69% of 72 benchmarks. They acknowledge that not all benchmarks improve and that the 1000-epoch cutoff is arbitrary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses extended epoch training and loss tracking to investigate epoch-wise double descent, but applies it to time-series Transformers and public forecasting benchmarks; the curve descriptions use validation loss, and the learning-rate schedule is held constant after epoch 5 rather than continuing its original exponential decay.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and model affect the observed trajectory: Autoformer on Exchange and Informer on ILI show a second descent, while Informer on Traffic remains overfitting through the 1000-epoch cutoff. FEDformer patience is reduced to 200 on Weather, ETTm1, and ETTm2.
record.problems: Only three Transformer families are tested, and training is limited to a 1000-epoch cutoff. The described curve results are validation-loss examples, not full test-error trajectories; uncertainty estimates are not reported in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports separate test-loss values across models, datasets, prediction lengths, and metrics. These endpoint comparisons do not show the epoch-wise curve shape and are not extracted individually; the paper's own aggregate FEDformer comparison is recorded in r4. No other curve values are stated numerically in the text.

untested.parts: Test-error (rather than validation-loss) trajectories; how often the shape occurs across all 36 model–benchmark runs per model; dependence on label noise; behaviour beyond 1000 epochs.
Training sample size is not varied.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
Label noise and regularization are not varied; no multiple-peak analysis.
No recounting of complexity via effective parameters.

missing.what: Text says some runs show 'double descents that remove the effects of overfitting but do not descend enough' to beat the first minimum. Figure 2 also shows runs in the classical regime with no second descent. No rows record these, and which models and datasets are affected is not specified.
Text says many models 'keep on improving (validation loss drops)' as epochs increase, i.e. monotone curves with no overfitting phase, across the Figure 2 panels for nine datasets.

record.verdict_notes: Curves are shown only as figures with a log-scale epoch axis. Numeric curve values are given only for Autoformer on Exchange. The learning-rate schedule is changed to stay constant after epoch 5, which may itself affect the curve shape. The double-descent examples are selected, and no prevalence is reported. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: The curve evidence is validation loss, not a full test-error trajectory; only selected examples are described, and training is cut off at 1000 epochs.
Training sample size is not varied near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes is performed.
No single effective-complexity measure is evaluated across axes.
The study does not vary label noise or regularization to assess peak dependence or multiple peaks.
The study does not recount complexity using an effective parameter measure.

rows.subject: Autoformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained for more epochs and monitored validation loss over training time.
rows.value: The loss deteriorated from below 1 to over 2 up to around epoch 100, then fell below its previous low point.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes an initial deterioration followed by a second descent below the previous minimum.

rows.subject: Informer
rows.operation_detail: Trained through the 1000-epoch cutoff and monitored validation loss.
rows.value: The model appears to keep overfitting up to the 1000-epoch cutoff; the authors say a second descent may occur later.
rows.note: No second descent is reported within the observed range; its possible occurrence after the cutoff is conjecture, not an observed result.
rows.check: State is correct only within the observed 1000-epoch range. The authors' claim that a second descent may come later is conjecture.

rows.subject: Informer
rows.operation_detail: Trained over epochs and monitored validation loss.
rows.value: The curve is described as having an initial descent, an overfitting phase, and a second descent.
rows.note: The paper describes the phases but does not provide numerical curve values in the text.

rows.subject: FEDformer
rows.operation_detail: Compared the original short training schema with extended training; the paper reports an aggregate benchmark summary.

conditions.value: 4 per dataset; ILI uses 24, 36, 48, and 60 time steps
original 10 epochs versus extended training, up to 1000 epochs; patience 200 for FEDformer on Weather, ETTm1, and ETTm2

rows.measure: Aggregate test performance comparison; MSE and MAE are reported in Table 1
rows.value: FEDformer improves in around 62.5% of benchmarks, with an average relative improvement of 6%; where performance does not improve, it deteriorates by 3%.
rows.note: This is the authors' aggregate summary of endpoint test results. It does not establish the fall-rise-fall shape over epochs.
rows.check: This compares endpoint test MSE/MAE of the extended-training schema against the original 10-epoch results. It is the study's own training-schema performance against a baseline and does not measure the epoch-wise curve shape, so it should not be linked to V2.

relationships.condition: Autoformer on Exchange; Informer on ILI at prediction length 336
